picks.name: Come Thru Black & Indigenous Market
picks.description: A vibrant marketplace of Black and Indigenous makers, artists, and vendors at Open Signal on MLK. Shop local, discover new creators, and support the community — all under one roof.

picks.name: The Moth StorySLAM: Magic
picks.description: The Moth's open-mic storytelling night comes to the Old Church with the theme "Magic." Put your name in the hat to tell a true five-minute story, or just come to listen — either way it's unforgettable.

picks.name: Counter Culture: Trade Day
picks.description: A full day bringing the cheese industry together at Bauman's on Oak — education, guided tastings, and networking with makers like Rogue Creamery, Vermont Creamery, and Le Gruyère AOP. A trade event for cheesemakers, mongers, and buyers.

picks.name: LØLØ
picks.description: Canadian pop-punk firecracker LØLØ brings her "God Forbid a Girl Goes on Tour" show to Holocene — sharp, funny, cathartic hooks you'll be screaming by the second chorus.

picks.name: Two Wheelin' in PDX Bike Ride
picks.description: A free, social group bike ride rolling out from the Jupiter Hotel. Easy pace, good company, and a fun way to see the city on two wheels — all riders welcome. Free Biketown rentals included for the event as well!

picks.name: A Dose of Burlesque: Halloween
picks.description: A free, spooky-season edition of The Pharmacy's burlesque revue — costumes, camp, and killer performances. Get there early; the good seats go fast.

picks.name: ReUse Open House
picks.description: The ReBuilding Center throws open its doors for a free open house — tour the salvaged-materials warehouse, meet the crew, and get inspired for your next reuse project.

picks.name: Stranger Things: The Musical Parody
picks.description: Funhouse Lounge turns Hawkins upside down with a loving musical parody of Stranger Things — Eleven, Demogorgons, and all. Campy, clever, and perfect for spooky season.

picks.name: Roux
picks.description: Every October, Roux celebrates food, drink, and culture while elevating women-owned businesses — pop-up dinners, chef collabs, panels, and brunch across the city. Explore the full lineup at rouxportland.com.

picks.name: The Taking of Portland 123
picks.description: Comedian Zak Toscani takes over the Portland Streetcar for a one-of-a-kind stand-up show rolling through the Central Eastside. An intimate, offbeat night — grab your seat before it departs. There are two shows, and they'll both sell out — get tickets soon!

picks.name: Occidental Oktoberfest
picks.description: North Portland's German brewery throws a free, family-friendly Oktoberfest — house-brewed lagers, brats, pretzels, and live music in the beer garden. Prost!

picks.name: Heartbeat Silent Disco: Mystery Ship Masquerade
picks.description: A masquerade silent disco aboard the Portland Spirit — three DJ channels on your headphones, masks on, cruising the Willamette after dark. A one-of-a-kind spooky-season night. 21+.

picks.name: Growing Garlic Made Simple
picks.description: Learn how to plant and grow your own garlic at this free class at Capitol Hill Library — perfect timing, since fall is the season to get cloves in the ground. Beginner-friendly and totally free.

picks.name: Practical Magic
picks.description: The cult witchy classic Practical Magic on the big screen at PAM CUT's Tomorrow Theater, part of their Witch Month. Gather your coven for a cozy, spellbinding Sunday night.
